title: India | RBI Compliance Function, Board Training and Workplace Conduct
tagline: Build the compliance culture RBI expects: train every employee, keep the CCO independent, keep directors fit and current, and speak up safely.
sectors: Foreign banks operating branches in India
Compliance, internal audit and risk functions of Indian banks
Boards, board committees and company secretariats of Indian banks
description:
This quest teaches the Reserve Bank of India's rules on compliance culture and governance for commercial banks. It is based on the **RBI (Commercial Banks - Compliance Function) Directions, 2026**, the **Internal Audit Function** and **Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026** (all issued on 31 July 2026 and effective on issue), and the **Miscellaneous** and **Governance Directions, 2025**, with the **POSH Act, 2013** in general terms.

RBI expects the need to comply to be reinforced for all staff through continuous and mandatory compliance training, need-based training for directors, periodic training for internal auditors and certification before posting to specialised areas. This quest supports those duties for all bank staff, compliance and audit teams, managers and directors.

In five stages you join the Compliance Department of a fictional Indian bank: compliance culture, the Compliance Department and CCO, the Board and fit and proper criteria, internal audit and certified staff, and speaking up with assessment readiness, illustrated by real RBI actions.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own compliance, audit, whistle-blower or POSH policies; always follow them and the latest RBI text.
audience: All staff of commercial banks in India, who must receive continuous and mandatory compliance training
Compliance Department staff, designated compliance officials in branches and business units, and aspiring CCOs
Board members, Nomination and Remuneration Committee members and company secretaries
Internal and concurrent auditors and the Head of Internal Audit
Managers of specialised areas such as treasury, risk, accounting, credit and third-party product sales
HR, vigilance and fraud risk staff who handle staff accountability, whistle-blower complaints and POSH matters
outcomes: Explain compliance risk and the roles of the Board, Audit Committee, senior management and staff under RBI's 2026 Compliance Function Directions
Apply the CCO's selection, tenure, reporting and independence rules and the compliance function's testing and review duties
Describe directors' training and familiarisation and run a fit and proper assessment for bank directors
Explain risk-based internal audit, auditor competence, certification before posting and mandatory leave rules
Raise and handle whistle-blower concerns about fraud and describe staff accountability and POSH duties in general terms
Assemble the evidence RBI will look for when it examines a bank's compliance culture

sessions.summary: What compliance risk means, which banks RBI's 2026 Compliance Function Directions cover, how the Board and senior management own compliance, and why RBI wants continuous, mandatory compliance training for all staff.
objectives: Define compliance risk in the words of RBI's 2026 Compliance Function Directions

cards.title: Day one: the training nobody finished
cards.setting: Compliance Department, Sahyadri Crest Bank head office, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai. 9:15 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Sahyadri Crest Bank, a fictional private sector commercial bank with branches across India, as its Compliance Training and Culture Officer.

Welcome! I'm Priya Venkataraman, the Chief Compliance Officer. RBI issued new Compliance Function Directions for commercial banks on 31 July 2026, effective the same day. You arrive at exactly the right time.
Thomas from Panaji, on video. Half my branch skipped the compliance module again. Honestly, isn't compliance your department's job, not ours?
Aditya, retail head. My teams have sales targets. A two-hour module every quarter feels like a luxury.
That is precisely the mindset RBI wants us to change. The new Directions say compliance must be a culture across the bank, backed by training that is continuous and mandatory.
Stage one is the Culture Gate: what compliance risk is, who owns it, and why every one of us must keep learning. Ready?

cards.title: Why RBI rewrote the compliance rulebook

scenes.heading: One set of Directions
scenes.narration: On 31 July 2026 RBI issued the Compliance Function Directions for commercial banks. They took effect immediately and replaced the earlier compliance instructions for these banks.

scenes.heading: Who is covered
scenes.narration: They apply to banking companies other than small finance, payments and local area banks, plus the nationalised banks and the State Bank of India.

scenes.heading: What compliance risk is
scenes.narration: Compliance risk is the chance that the bank suffers legal or regulatory sanctions, a material financial loss or damage to its reputation because it failed to follow the laws, rules, standards and codes that apply to it.

scenes.heading: Built on Basel
scenes.narration: RBI says the principles follow the Basel Committee's framework for compliance, adapted to India, and that each bank should scale its function to its size, complexity and risk profile.

scenes.heading: Culture, not a department
scenes.narration: The Directions say compliance should pervade the whole bank. Staff must be reminded regularly, through continuous and mandatory training, to follow instructions carefully.

cards.title: Who owns compliance at the bank
cards.caption: Built from Chapters II and III of the Compliance Function Directions, 2026.

items.label: Board of Directors
items.detail: Overall oversight of compliance risk; approves the compliance policy and reviews it at least once a year

items.label: Audit Committee of the Board
items.detail: May take delegated tasks; with the Board, reviews the compliance function every quarter, plus a detailed annual review

items.label: MD & CEO and senior management
items.detail: Keep the function independent, write the policy, assess main compliance risks yearly and act on breaches

items.label: CCO and Compliance Department
items.detail: Identify, test and report compliance risk; vet circulars; train and advise staff

items.label: Every employee
items.detail: Follows instructions meticulously, completes compliance training and raises concerns

cards.question: Which of these institutions is covered by RBI's Compliance Function Directions, 2026 for commercial banks?
options: A small finance bank licensed by RBI
A nationalised bank with branches across India
A payments bank licensed by RBI
A local area bank in one region
cards.explanation: The Directions cover banking companies other than small finance, payments and local area banks, plus corresponding new (nationalised) banks and SBI. The excluded categories have their own instructions.

cards.title: What the Board and senior management must do
cards.body:
**The Board** carries overall responsibility for overseeing the compliance function and compliance risk. It makes sure a suitable compliance policy exists, oversees how it is applied and **reviews it at least once a year**. It may delegate the job of getting issues resolved to the **Audit Committee of the Board (ACB)**.

**Reviews:** the Board or ACB reviews the compliance function **every quarter**, with a detailed **annual review** as well. The CCO is invited to these meetings.

**Separation:** the Board keeps the compliance and internal audit functions **separate**.

**The MD & CEO** ensures an independent compliance function exists and that the policy is followed.

**Senior management** writes the compliance policy, identifies and assesses the main compliance risks **at least yearly**, reports any material compliance failure to the Board or ACB promptly, and makes sure remedial or disciplinary action follows when breaches are found.

cards.title: Match the role to its duty
cards.prompt: Link each role to one of its duties under the 2026 Compliance Function Directions.

pairs.right: Reviews the compliance policy at least once a year and keeps compliance separate from internal audit
Reviews the compliance function every quarter and receives a detailed annual review
Ensures there is an independent compliance function and that the policy is followed
Reports any material compliance failure to the Board or ACB promptly and takes remedial steps
Vets the bank's own circulars against regulatory guidelines before they go out to units

cards.title: The circular in the drawer
cards.setting: Panaji branch, Goa. A week later, during your first branch visit.

lines.text: Good timing. Head office sent a circular on a new RBI instruction three weeks ago. It is still in my inbox, unread by the counter staff.
A customer complaint has just arrived: the branch applied the old rule, not the new one.
We were busy with year-end. I thought someone would explain it at the next staff meeting.
(on the phone) RBI expects circulars to reach the field without delay and to be implemented quickly. And our own Directions say compliance is everyone's job, not something that waits for a meeting.
So what should I have done the day it arrived?

cards.title: The new circular arrives
cards.situation: A head office circular, already vetted by Compliance, explains a change in an RBI instruction that affects how the Panaji counter handles a common customer request. Thomas is busy, staff are stretched, and the next scheduled staff meeting is two weeks away.

choices.text: Brief the affected staff the same day, confirm they understood the change, update the desk procedure and ask Compliance about anything unclear.
choices.outcome: Best. The Miscellaneous Directions want RBI instructions implemented at field level without delay, and the Compliance Department is the staff's reference point for interpretation. The branch now applies the new rule from day one.

choices.text: Forward the circular to all staff by email and ask them to read it when they can.
choices.outcome: Partly right. The information reaches staff, but nobody checks understanding or changes the procedure, so the old practice may continue.

choices.text: Wait for the staff meeting in two weeks so everyone hears it together.
choices.outcome: Poor. Two more weeks of the old rule means more breaches and complaints. RBI expects speedy implementation, not convenience.

choices.text: Apply the change only for customers who ask about it.
choices.outcome: Poor. A regulatory instruction applies to every relevant case, not just to customers who know about it. This creates unequal treatment and a compliance breach.

cards.title: How a compliance culture keeps itself alive
cards.caption: Drawn from paragraphs 30, 33, 44 and 52 of the Compliance Function Directions.

items.label: Train continuously
items.detail: Continuous and mandatory compliance training reminds all staff to follow instructions meticulously

items.label: Share instructions fast
items.detail: Vetted circulars and updated manuals reach operational staff promptly

items.label: Learn from failures
items.detail: Compliance circulates instances of compliance failures with preventive instructions

items.label: Hold people accountable
items.detail: Staff accountability is examined for compliance failures, with disciplinary measures where due

items.label: Reward clean records
items.detail: Compliance records can carry weight in performance appraisal at every level

cards.title: Culture builder or culture breaker?
cards.prompt: Sort each practice by whether it builds or weakens the compliance culture RBI expects.

items.text: Branch staff complete the mandatory compliance module on time
A manager tells staff that compliance is the Compliance Department's problem
Compliance shares anonymised breach examples with preventive tips
A top seller with repeated breaches gets the best appraisal rating anyway
Staff ask Compliance to interpret a confusing instruction before acting
A circular waits unread for weeks because the branch is busy
The bank examines staff accountability after a compliance failure
Training is skipped every quarter during sales campaigns

cards.title: Real case: Paytm Payments Bank, 2022 to 2024
cards.body:
In **March 2022** RBI used its powers under **Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949** to stop Paytm Payments Bank from onboarding new customers.

On **31 January 2024** RBI said the bank's comprehensive system audit report and the external auditors' later compliance validation report showed **persistent non-compliances and continued material supervisory concerns**. It barred further deposits, credits and top-ups to customer accounts, wallets and FASTags after a cut-off date (later extended to 15 March 2024), while customers could still withdraw their balances.

A payments bank is outside the 2026 Directions for commercial banks, but the lesson carries across: **a compliance gap that is reported but not fixed turns into business restrictions** that hurt customers and the franchise.

*Source: RBI press releases of 31 January 2024 and 16 February 2024.*

cards.front: Myth: compliance is the Compliance Department's job.
cards.back: RBI says compliance should not be seen as the department's job alone but as a culture across the whole bank.

cards.front: Myth: one induction session is enough.
cards.back: RBI asks for continuous and mandatory compliance training so the message is repeated to all staff over time.

cards.front: Myth: breaches only matter if RBI finds them.
cards.back: The bank must examine staff accountability for all compliance failures and disclose regulatory non-compliance in its annual report.

cards.front: Myth: appraisals are about sales only.
cards.back: RBI suggests giving due weight to each employee's compliance record in performance appraisal.

cards.front: Fact or myth: Compliance must vet internal circulars.
cards.back: Fact. Compliance vets the bank's own circulars against regulatory guidelines before they are sent to operating units.

cards.question: According to the 2026 Directions, how should the need to comply with instructions be reinforced across the bank?
options: Through an annual email from the CCO that staff may acknowledge if they wish
Through training for Compliance Department staff only, who then answer queries
Repeated periodically to all staff through continuous, mandatory compliance training and a staff accountability framework
Through disciplinary action alone, without any training requirement
cards.explanation: Paragraph 52 combines continuous and mandatory training for all staff with disciplinary measures under a staff accountability framework. Training only the Compliance Department misses the point that compliance is a bank-wide culture.

cards.title: Making training stick at your branch
cards.body:
- **Schedule it like a sales review.** Block time for the compliance module so campaigns do not crowd it out.
- **Use real breach stories.** The Compliance Department circulates instances of failures; discuss one at each team huddle.
- **Check understanding, not attendance.** A short quiz or a role-play shows whether staff can apply a new instruction.
- **Track completion.** Your appraisal and your team's may reflect compliance records.

cards.title: Stage one: the Culture Gate
items: RBI's Compliance Function Directions, 2026 took effect on 31 July 2026 for commercial banks other than small finance, payments and local area banks.
Compliance risk is the risk of sanctions, material financial loss or reputational damage from failing to follow applicable laws, rules, standards and codes.
The Board reviews the compliance policy at least yearly; the Board or ACB reviews the function quarterly, with a detailed annual review.
All staff must be reminded through continuous and mandatory compliance training, backed by staff accountability.
Compliance is a culture across the bank, supported by fast circulation of instructions and appraisals that value compliance.

cards.prompt: Think of the last regulatory change that reached your team. How long did it take to reach the people who apply it, and what would you change so it arrives and sticks faster?

quiz.question: Which definition best matches 'compliance risk' in RBI's Compliance Function Directions, 2026?
options: The risk that borrowers fail to repay loans because of weak credit appraisal by business lines
The risk of loss from failed internal processes, people and systems, including cyber attacks
The risk that the Compliance Department exceeds its budget for monitoring tools and staff
The risk of legal or regulatory sanctions, material financial loss or reputational damage from failing to follow applicable laws, rules, standards and codes
quiz.explanation: The Directions define compliance risk by its consequences (sanctions, material loss, reputational harm) and its cause (failure to comply). Operational risk overlaps but is a broader category, and credit risk is a different risk type.

quiz.question: A bank's Board wants to know how often it must review the compliance policy under the 2026 Directions. What is the minimum?
options: At least once every three years
At least once a year
Only when RBI raises an observation
At least once every quarter
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7 requires the Board to review the compliance policy at least annually. The quarterly cycle applies to the Board or ACB review of the compliance function, not to the policy.

quiz.question: The Audit Committee of Sahyadri Crest Bank reviews the compliance function. Which pattern meets the 2026 Directions?
options: A review every quarter plus a detailed annual review, with the CCO invited
One review a year, with the CCO absent to keep the discussion frank
A review every six months, with the Head of Internal Audit presenting for Compliance
Reviews only after a material compliance failure has been reported
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 9 sets quarterly reviews of the compliance function and a detailed annual review, with the CCO as an invitee. Having Internal Audit present for Compliance would blur the separation the Board must keep.

quiz.question: Thomas says compliance is 'Head Office's job'. Which statement from the 2026 Directions best answers him?
options: Compliance belongs to branch managers, who report breaches directly to RBI
Compliance is the Board's job, so staff only need to follow sales targets
Compliance is a culture that should pervade the whole bank, not the Compliance Department's responsibility alone
Compliance belongs to Internal Audit, which tests every branch once a year
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 52 says compliance should not be seen as the Compliance Department's job alone but as a culture across the bank. Branch staff do not report directly to RBI; the CCO is the nodal point.

quiz.question: Aditya proposes skipping the quarterly compliance module during a deposit campaign. Which RBI expectation does this conflict with most directly?
options: That every product launch is cleared by the Board of Directors before marketing begins
That the need to comply is reiterated to all staff through continuous and mandatory training on compliance
That sales staff hold a certificate before selling the bank's own deposit products
That the CCO must personally deliver training at every branch each quarter
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 52 calls for continuous and mandatory compliance training for all staff. New products need Compliance clearance, not Board clearance of each launch, and the Directions do not require the CCO to train in person.

quiz.question: A branch receives a vetted circular on a changed RBI instruction. What does RBI expect about its implementation?
options: It may wait until the next quarterly staff meeting so all staff hear it together
It applies only after the branch's next internal audit confirms it is relevant
It should reach the field without delay and be put into practice speedily
It applies only to customers who ask about the new rule at the counter
quiz.explanation: The Miscellaneous Directions ask banks to circulate RBI circulars without delay and ensure speedy field implementation. Waiting for a meeting or an audit leaves customers exposed to the old practice.

quiz.question: Which of these is a duty of senior management under the 2026 Directions?
options: Approve each internal circular personally before Compliance sees it
Conduct the independent external review of the compliance function
Set business targets for the CCO linked to retail deposit growth
Identify and assess the bank's main compliance risks at least once a year and plan how to manage them
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 14 asks senior management, with the compliance function, to assess the main compliance risks at least annually. Business targets for the CCO are prohibited, and the external review must be independent.

quiz.question: What must happen when senior management learns of a material compliance failure that could attract significant regulatory sanctions?
options: Report it promptly to the Board or ACB and take appropriate remedial measures
Hold it until the annual review so the Board sees all failures together
Report it only if the loss exceeds a threshold that RBI publishes each year
Fix it quietly at branch level and record it in the branch diary
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 14(3) requires prompt reporting of material compliance failures to the Board or ACB with remedial action. The Directions set no published loss threshold for this duty.

quiz.question: Under the 2026 Directions, how should a bank treat compliance records in staff management?
options: Keep compliance records out of appraisals so that staff report breaches freely
Give due weight to compliance records in performance appraisal and examine staff accountability for compliance failures
Use compliance records only for staff in the Compliance Department
Consider compliance records only when RBI has imposed a penalty
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 44 suggests due weight for compliance records in appraisals at all levels and requires staff accountability for all compliance failures. Limiting it to Compliance staff or to penalty cases would weaken the culture.

quiz.question: In January 2024 RBI barred further deposits and credits at Paytm Payments Bank after a cut-off date. What reason did RBI give?
options: Audit reports showed persistent non-compliances and continued material supervisory concerns
The bank had failed to appoint a Chief Compliance Officer within the time allowed
The bank's capital had fallen below the minimum and depositors were withdrawing funds
The bank had been merged into a larger bank under an RBI scheme
quiz.explanation: RBI's 31 January 2024 press release cited the system audit report and the external auditors' compliance validation report showing persistent non-compliances and continued material supervisory concerns. It did not cite a CCO vacancy or a capital shortfall.

sessions.summary: How the Compliance Department is staffed, trained and kept independent, what the Chief Compliance Officer must be and do, and how compliance testing, new product approval, annual reviews and RBI follow-up work in practice.

cards.title: A tidy reorganisation?
cards.setting: Board room, 22nd floor, Mumbai. The quarterly Audit Committee meeting is ending.

lines.text: Gurpreet Singh Bedi, chair of the Audit Committee. Aditya has a proposal before we close.
Simple: Priya reports to me, she joins the credit sanction committee as a voting member, and she gets a target for new digital accounts. Compliance and business, one team.
One team on culture, yes. But if I report to the business I check, and I vote on loans I may later have to challenge, my independence is gone.
Fatima, internal audit. Some of Aditya's staff even suggested Compliance could help us with branch inspections to save time.
Before we vote on anything, I want to see what the new Directions say. Can you two brief us?

scenes.heading: A department at the top
scenes.narration: Each bank sets up a Compliance Department at its head office, headed by the Chief Compliance Officer. Foreign banks set it up at their controlling office in India.

scenes.heading: Compliance everywhere
scenes.narration: Head office departments, controlling offices, branches and business units each have designated compliance officials who report to the CCO.

scenes.heading: Never audit duty
scenes.narration: Compliance staff must never be given audit or inspection duty. Compliance clears products and processes, so their audit must be done by a separate team.

scenes.heading: Pay without bias
scenes.narration: Compliance staff pay must not depend on the business line they oversee, though it can reflect the bank's overall results.

scenes.heading: Skilled and current
scenes.narration: Compliance staff should know law, accounting and technology, and banks may consider regular, systematic training on new products, governance, risk and supervisory practice.

cards.title: Compliance and Internal Audit: separate by design
cards.caption: From the Compliance Function and Internal Audit Function Directions, 2026.

items.label: Purpose
items.left: Identifies, assesses, tests and advises on compliance risk
items.right: Gives independent assurance on risk management and controls

items.label: New products
items.left: Approves new products and processes before launch

items.label: Head
items.left: CCO, fixed tenure of at least three years
items.right: Head of Internal Audit, preferably at least three years

items.label: Who reviews whom
items.left: Is itself subject to internal audit
items.right: Covers compliance adequacy in its audit programme

items.label: Staffing rule
items.left: Never assigned audit or inspection duty
items.right: Not given accounting or operational duties

cards.question: Fatima's team is short of inspectors. Can Priya lend two compliance officers to inspect branches this quarter?
options: Yes, if the CCO approves it in writing and the loan lasts under three months
Yes, provided the compliance officers inspect branches outside their own region
No. Compliance staff must never be given audit or inspection duty, because their own clearances need independent audit
cards.explanation: Paragraph 24 says that under no circumstances should compliance staff be given audit or inspection duty. Neither a time limit nor a regional rotation removes the conflict.

cards.title: The CCO: who can be appointed
cards.body:
**Selection:** a senior executive selection committee set up by the Board recommends candidates in order of merit after a **fit and proper** assessment (competence, integrity, conflicts of interest). The **Board decides**. The CCO may be recruited from outside.

**Clean record:** no vigilance case or adverse RBI observation pending against the candidate.

**Age:** not more than **55** at appointment, unless the person has been continuously associated with compliance since before turning 55.

**Experience:** at least **15 years** in banking or financial services, with at least **five years** in audit, finance, compliance, legal or risk management (control functions in business lines count).

**Rank:** a senior executive, preferably General Manager or equivalent, **not more than two levels below the MD & CEO**.

**RBI:** the bank tells RBI's **Senior Supervisory Manager in advance** of an appointment or a premature transfer or removal, with the candidate's profile and the MD & CEO's fit and proper certificate.

cards.title: The CCO in numbers
cards.caption: Chapter IV of the Compliance Function Directions, 2026.

items.label: Minimum tenure
items.detail: Earlier transfer or removal only in exceptional cases with the Board's explicit prior approval

items.label: Total experience
items.detail: In banking or financial services, at least five of them in control functions

items.label: Age at appointment
items.detail: Unless continuously in the compliance function since before turning 55

items.label: Rank
items.detail: Preferably General Manager or equivalent, not below two levels from the MD & CEO

items.label: ACB one-to-one
items.detail: If the CCO reports to the MD & CEO, the ACB meets the CCO alone each quarter

cards.title: Briefing the Audit Committee
cards.situation: Gurpreet asks you to recommend a response to Aditya's three proposals: the CCO reports to the Head of Retail Banking, sits as a voting member on the credit sanction committee, and receives a digital account opening target.

choices.text: Reject all three: the CCO reports directly to the MD & CEO and/or Board or ACB, has no business targets, and sits on conflicting committees only as an adviser.
choices.outcome: Best. The Directions bar any reporting line to business verticals and any business targets, and limit the CCO to an advisory role on committees, such as sanction committees, that create a conflict.

choices.text: Accept the reporting line but drop the target, since targets are the real problem.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Dropping the target helps, but a reporting line to a business vertical is itself prohibited and would let the business shape compliance findings.

choices.text: Accept all three for a one-year trial and review the effect on approvals.
choices.outcome: Poor. A trial does not make a prohibited arrangement acceptable. RBI could see it as a breach of the CCO independence rules from day one.

choices.text: Let the CCO vote on credit sanctions but recuse herself from large loans.
choices.outcome: Poor. On a committee dealing with sanctions, the CCO may only advise. Partial recusal still makes her a decision maker in matters she may need to challenge.

cards.title: Allowed or not allowed for the CCO?
cards.prompt: Sort each arrangement under the 2026 Compliance Function Directions.

items.text: Reporting directly to the MD & CEO, with quarterly one-to-one ACB meetings
A target for new digital account openings
Acting as anti-money laundering officer where size and proportionality justify it
A reporting line to the Head of Retail Banking
Membership of the new product committee
Voting on the purchase committee for IT contracts
Appraisal reviewed by the Board or ACB
Removal after one year because business heads find her strict

cards.title: The product launch on Monday
cards.setting: Product committee room, Mumbai. Friday, 6 pm.

lines.text: Our new instant overdraft for small traders goes live on Monday. Marketing has already booked the billboards.
Has the product come to Compliance for clearance? I have seen the brochure, not the process notes.
It is basically an old product with a new app. Can't you sign off this evening?
The Directions want compliance risks in every new product analysed and mitigants in place before launch, and then six months of intensive monitoring. Let's look at it properly.

cards.title: From idea to launch: the compliance path
cards.prompt: Put the steps for a new product in the order the 2026 Directions imply.
steps: The business line proposes the product to the new product committee, where the CCO is a member
Compliance identifies and assesses the product's compliance risks against laws, rules and codes
Checks and balances are designed and put in place to mitigate those risks
Compliance clears the product and process before introduction
The product launches and staff receive the related compliance guidance
The bank monitors the product intensively for its first six months

cards.title: The compliance programme in practice
cards.body:
**Risk-based programme:** compliance activities run under a planned, risk-based programme overseen by the CCO, with compliance testing and review built in.

**Testing:** Compliance tests compliance using sufficient, representative samples and places the results before the Board, ACB or MD & CEO. It can use indicators to measure compliance risk.

**Manuals:** function-wise compliance manuals, approved by the CCO, where operating manuals lack compliance chapters.

**Annual review:** an annual compliance risk assessment and review covering failures and losses, major new regulations, independence, internal controls, progress on audit and RBI findings, and next year's plan, including staff training.

**Monthly view:** a monthly report on compliance risk may go to senior management or the MD & CEO.

**Quality:** a quality assurance programme with an **independent external review at least once in three years**.

**Technology:** an integrated, workflow-based tool that escalates non-compliance, records approvals for delays and gives senior management one dashboard.

cards.title: Real case: Kotak Mahindra Bank, April 2024
cards.body:
On **24 April 2024** RBI used **Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949** to stop Kotak Mahindra Bank from onboarding new customers through online and mobile channels and from issuing new credit cards.

RBI's IT examinations for **2022 and 2023** had found serious deficiencies in areas such as IT inventory, patch and change management, user access, vendor risk, data leak prevention and disaster recovery. RBI said the bank was significantly non-compliant with the **corrective action plans** it had issued, because the compliance submitted was **inadequate, incorrect or not sustained**.

**The lesson for the compliance function:** reporting that a supervisory finding is closed is not the same as fixing it. The 2026 Directions make the CCO responsible for complying with supervisory observations in letter and spirit, on time and in a sustainable way.

*Source: RBI press release, 24 April 2024.*

cards.prompt: Match each supervisory touchpoint to what the 2026 Directions require.

The CCO must take part; if none is held, the CCO meets the RBI official in charge each quarter

options: The MD & CEO sends RBI a monthly certificate confirming the CCO's independence
The CCO's appraisal is written by the Head of Retail Banking for balance
The Head of Internal Audit attends every meeting between the CCO and the MD & CEO
The Audit Committee meets the CCO one-to-one every quarter without senior management present
cards.explanation: Paragraph 65 says that where the CCO reports to the MD & CEO, the ACB meets the CCO quarterly on a one-to-one basis without senior management, including the MD & CEO. The CCO's appraisal is reviewed by the Board or ACB, never by a business head.

cards.title: Stage two: the Watchtower
items: Every bank has a head office Compliance Department led by the CCO, with designated compliance officials across offices and branches.
Compliance staff are never given audit or inspection duty, and their pay does not depend on the business line they cover.
The CCO: fit and proper selection, at least 15 years' experience, at most 55 at appointment, a fixed tenure of at least three years, and no business reporting line or targets.
New products need compliance clearance before launch and six months of intensive monitoring afterwards.
The CCO is RBI's nodal contact and must make sure supervisory findings are fixed in a sustainable way.

cards.prompt: If you had to explain to a business head why the CCO cannot report to them, which two arguments from this stage would you use, and how would you keep the relationship cooperative?

quiz.question: Which candidate meets the CCO experience rule in the 2026 Directions?
options: Twelve years in banking, all of them in compliance at head office
Twenty years in banking, all in branch sales with no control function role
Fifteen years in a technology firm, five of them in its legal team
Sixteen years in banking, including six years as a zonal head responsible for control functions in business lines
quiz.explanation: The CCO needs at least 15 years in banking or financial services, with at least five in audit, finance, compliance, legal or risk management; control functions within business lines count. Twelve years falls short, and a technology firm is not banking or financial services.

quiz.question: A bank wants to appoint a 58-year-old outsider who has never worked in compliance as CCO. What do the 2026 Directions say?
options: Eligible, because the age limit applies only to candidates promoted from within the bank
Eligible if RBI's Senior Supervisory Manager is informed after the appointment
Not eligible: the CCO must be no older than 55 at appointment unless continuously associated with compliance since before 55
Eligible, because the Directions set only a minimum age of 35 for the CCO
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 58 caps the age at 55 at appointment, with an exception only for continuous association with the compliance function from before 55. Intimation to RBI must come before the appointment, not after.

quiz.question: Two years into a three-year CCO tenure, the MD & CEO wants to move the CCO to a business role. What is required?
options: Only the MD & CEO's written order, because the CCO reports to the MD & CEO
Approval of the Head of Internal Audit and notice to the Compliance Department
Nothing special, as long as the replacement CCO meets the experience rules
Exceptional circumstances, the Board's explicit prior approval, a transparent procedure and prior intimation to RBI
quiz.explanation: Paragraphs 62 and 70 allow premature transfer or removal only in exceptional cases, with explicit prior Board approval after a transparent procedure, and with prior intimation to RBI's Senior Supervisory Manager. The MD & CEO cannot decide alone.

quiz.question: Which committee role is consistent with the CCO's independence?
options: Voting member of the credit sanction committee for large corporate loans
Voting member of the purchase committee for technology contracts
Member of the new product committee, to make sure products are cleared from a compliance view
Chair of the retail sales committee that sets branch targets
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 makes the CCO a member of new product committees; paragraph 68 limits the CCO to an advisory role on committees that create conflicts, such as purchase or sanction committees. Chairing a sales committee is a business role.

quiz.question: A large bank asks whether its CCO may also act as its anti-money laundering officer. What is the best answer?
options: Possibly, since that role does not create a direct conflict, where the bank's size and proportionality justify it
Never, because any additional role is 'dual hatting' and is prohibited
Yes, and the CCO may also head the treasury desk if the Board agrees
Only if the CCO gives up the reporting line to the Board or ACB
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 67 bans roles that bring conflicts, especially business roles, but says roles without direct conflict, such as AML officer, may be performed by the CCO where proportionality justifies it. Heading treasury is a business role.

quiz.question: A new credit product launched last month. What monitoring do the 2026 Directions require?
options: A single post-launch review by Internal Audit after twelve months
Intensive monitoring for the first six months so that indicators of compliance risk are watched closely
Monitoring only if customers complain within the first ninety days
No extra monitoring, because the product was cleared before launch
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 35 requires intensive monitoring of all new products for the first six months. Clearance before launch does not remove the need to watch how the product behaves in practice.

quiz.question: Which statement about the annual compliance review is correct?
options: It is prepared by Internal Audit and covers only the previous year's RBI penalties
It replaces the quarterly reviews, so the Board sees compliance once a year
It covers failures and losses, major new regulations, independence, progress on audit and RBI findings, and next year's plan including training
It is sent to RBI instead of the Board, which does not review compliance
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 47 lists the contents of the annual review, including posting, transfer and training of staff in next year's strategy. It adds to, rather than replaces, the quarterly reviews of paragraph 9.

quiz.question: How often must the compliance function's quality assurance programme be reviewed externally?
options: Independently and externally at least once in three years
Every year, by the bank's statutory auditor
Every five years, by RBI's inspection team
Only when the CCO changes
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 53 requires a quality assurance and improvement programme with an independent external review periodically, at least once in three years.

quiz.question: RBI held no quarterly informal discussion with Sahyadri Crest Bank this quarter. What must the CCO do?
options: Nothing, because the discussion is informal and optional for both sides
Meet the Chief General Manager in charge of the bank at RBI's Department of Supervision to discuss compliance issues
Write to the Board explaining that RBI did not call the meeting
Ask the Head of Internal Audit to represent the bank at the next meeting
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 73 says that if no quarterly meeting is held, the CCO meets the CGM in charge of the bank at RBI's central office every quarter. The CCO is the bank's nodal contact with RBI.

quiz.question: RBI's April 2024 action against Kotak Mahindra Bank highlights which failure most relevant to a CCO?
options: A CCO who had been appointed without RBI's prior approval
A failure to set up a Compliance Department at the head office
A board that had not met for more than a year
Compliance with RBI's corrective action plans that was inadequate, incorrect or not sustained
quiz.explanation: RBI's press release said the bank was significantly non-compliant with the corrective action plans for 2022 and 2023, as compliance submitted was inadequate, incorrect or not sustained. It did not mention the CCO's appointment or board meetings.

sessions.title: The Board: Directors' Training, Familiarisation and Fit and Proper Criteria
sessions.summary: What RBI expects directors to know, how banks must train and familiarise them, and how the Nomination and Remuneration Committee tests directors against fit and proper criteria, with lessons from Yes Bank and Lakshmi Vilas Bank.
objectives: Explain the director training and awareness duties in paragraph 58 of the Miscellaneous Directions
Describe the familiarisation of public sector bank directors before induction
Apply the fit and proper process and criteria for private sector bank directors
Draw governance lessons from RBI's 2020 actions on Yes Bank and Lakshmi Vilas Bank

cards.title: A new director, a thin induction pack
cards.setting: Company Secretary's office, Mumbai. The week before the Board meeting.

lines.text: We have a new independent director joining next month, a well-known agricultural economist. Our induction pack is a 300-page PDF and a lunch.
And the existing directors? When did they last get a session on new technology risks or the 2026 Directions?
Honestly, not since the pandemic. Some of us think training is for staff, not directors.
RBI disagrees. The Miscellaneous Directions ask banks to design need-based training for directors, and the Board itself must keep directors current.
Then help me design it. And the Nomination Committee wants a refresher on fit and proper checks before it clears the new director.

scenes.heading: Need-based training
scenes.narration: Paragraph 58 of RBI's Miscellaneous Directions asks banks to design need-based training programmes, seminars or workshops to keep directors aware of new developments and challenges in banking.

scenes.heading: Technology and controls
scenes.narration: Banks must also raise senior management's awareness of security, risk and controls in a computerised environment.

scenes.heading: The Board's own duty
scenes.narration: The Board must make sure directors are exposed to the latest management techniques, banking technology, financial markets and risk management systems, so they can do their jobs well.

scenes.heading: Foreign banks
scenes.narration: RBI says this director training requirement is not insisted upon for foreign banks operating in India.

scenes.heading: Public sector banks
scenes.narration: In public sector banks, every director must be familiarised with how the bank works before induction, covering delegated powers, strategy, structure, controls and the market.

cards.title: Familiarising a public sector bank director before induction
cards.caption: The five areas in paragraph 9 of the Governance Directions, 2025.

items.label: Delegation of powers
items.detail: Which authorities the Board has delegated, and to whom

items.label: Strategic plan
items.detail: Where the bank intends to go and how

items.label: Organisation structure
items.detail: How the bank is organised and who is accountable

items.label: Controls and systems
items.detail: Financial and other controls and systems in place

items.label: Market and competition
items.detail: Economic features of the market and the competitive environment

cards.question: Which statement about director training matches paragraph 58 of the Miscellaneous Directions?
options: Directors must pass an RBI examination before their first Board meeting
Training is optional for directors, because only staff need compliance training
Directors must attend the same branch compliance module as counter staff each quarter
Banks must design need-based training for directors, and the Board must keep directors exposed to current techniques, technology, markets and risk systems
cards.explanation: Paragraph 58 places duties on the bank (need-based programmes) and on the Board (keeping directors current). It does not set an RBI examination or require directors to sit staff modules.

cards.title: Fit and proper: the process in a private sector bank
cards.body:
**Due diligence** happens when a director is appointed or re-appointed. The bank tests suitability on **qualification, expertise, track record, integrity** and other fit and proper criteria.

**Declaration and undertaking:** proposed and existing directors give information in the format RBI annexes to the Governance Directions.

**The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC)** scrutinises the declaration and decides on acceptance, making further enquiries where needed.

**Integrity checks** consider criminal records, financial position, civil actions over personal debts, refusal or expulsion by professional bodies, regulatory sanctions and questionable past business practices.

**No judging your own case:** the Board itself carries out due diligence on NRC members, and an NRC member who proposed or seconded a candidate stays out of that candidate's assessment; the Board names a temporary member instead.

**Every year:** a deed of covenant and a declaration that nothing has changed, as on 31 March, and a certificate to RBI that continuing due diligence was done.

cards.title: Fit and proper markers for non-executive directors
cards.caption: Private sector banks, paragraph 44 of the Governance Directions, 2025.

items.label: Minimum age
items.detail: Upper limit of 75 for non-executive directors, including the Chair

items.label: Education
items.detail: Can be relaxed for categories such as farmers, depositors and artisans

items.label: Special knowledge
items.detail: Share of the Board with special knowledge or experience in listed fields, under the Banking Regulation Act

items.label: Total tenure
items.detail: Then a gap of at least three years before re-appointment to the same bank

cards.title: Does it matter for the fit and proper test?
cards.prompt: Sort each fact about a proposed director of a private sector bank.

items.text: A pending civil suit over unpaid personal debts
Expulsion from a professional accountancy body
A past penalty imposed by a financial regulator
The candidate is a sitting Member of a Legislative Assembly
The candidate supports a particular cricket team
The candidate prefers to attend meetings by video
Ten years already served as a non-executive director of this bank
The candidate's preferred language is Marathi

cards.title: The proposer on the committee
cards.setting: Nomination and Remuneration Committee meeting, Mumbai.

lines.text: The NRC is reviewing the agricultural economist's declaration. One NRC member, Mr Rao, proposed her name to the Board.
Mr Rao knows her best. Surely he should lead the review?
The Directions say the opposite. A member who proposed or seconded the name stays out of that due diligence, and the Board names another director as a temporary member.
And her declaration mentions a regulatory penalty from her time on a fintech board. Do we just accept her explanation?

cards.title: The declaration with a red flag
cards.situation: The candidate's declaration discloses a penalty a financial regulator imposed on a company where she was a non-executive director, and a civil suit by a lender over a personal loan that she says is settled. The NRC meets tomorrow. Mr Rao has been replaced by a temporary member for this item.

choices.text: Ask for documents on the penalty and the suit, make references to the relevant authorities if needed, record the discussion in minutes, then decide.
choices.outcome: Best. The NRC may make references to appropriate authorities and must weigh regulatory sanctions and civil actions over personal debts. Recording the reasoning shows a real fit and proper test.

choices.text: Accept her explanation, since she is highly qualified and the suit is settled.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Her expertise matters, but the NRC should verify integrity factors rather than rely on assurance alone.

choices.text: Reject her automatically because any regulatory penalty disqualifies a director.
choices.outcome: Poor. The Directions list sanctions as factors to consider, not as automatic bars. A blanket rejection skips the judgement the NRC is meant to exercise.

choices.text: Let Mr Rao rejoin for this item, since he knows the facts best.
choices.outcome: Poor. A proposer must stay out of the due diligence on that candidate. His knowledge can be shared as information, not as a vote.

cards.title: Real cases: Yes Bank and Lakshmi Vilas Bank, 2020
cards.body:
**Yes Bank, March 2020.** RBI said the bank's financial position had declined steadily because it could not raise capital, and that it had also experienced **serious governance issues and practices in recent years**. With no credible revival plan, the Central Government imposed a moratorium on **5 March 2020** and RBI **superseded the Board for 30 days**, appointing an Administrator under the Banking Regulation Act.

**Lakshmi Vilas Bank, November 2020.** RBI cited three years of losses, no viable strategic plan, mounting NPAs, failure to raise capital and **serious governance issues and practices**. On **17 November 2020** a moratorium was imposed, the Board was superseded for 30 days and RBI published a draft scheme to amalgamate the bank with DBS Bank India.

**The lesson:** directors who do not challenge strategy, capital and controls can lose the Board altogether.

*Sources: RBI press releases, 5 March 2020 and 17 November 2020.*

cards.title: When governance fails: RBI actions on boards
cards.caption: From RBI press releases.

items.label: Yes Bank moratorium
items.detail: Board superseded for 30 days; RBI cited serious governance issues and inability to raise capital

items.label: Yes Bank reconstruction
items.detail: RBI published a draft reconstruction scheme with State Bank of India as investor

items.label: Lakshmi Vilas Bank moratorium
items.detail: Board superseded for 30 days; RBI cited losses, NPAs and serious governance issues

items.label: LVB amalgamation draft
items.detail: RBI proposed amalgamation with DBS Bank India Ltd

cards.title: Board training and fitness: quick facts

cards.back: The bank designs need-based training programmes, seminars or workshops; the Board ensures directors stay current.
The Board carries out due diligence on NRC members; they do not assess themselves.
Each private sector bank director signs a deed of covenant and a declaration that earlier information has not changed.

cards.front: What goes to RBI each year?
cards.back: A certificate from the private sector bank that it carried out continuing due diligence on its directors.
Between 35 and 67 years on the cut-off date for nominations, along with being at least a graduate.

cards.front: Can an MP or MLA be a non-executive director of a private bank?
cards.back: No. A Member of Parliament, Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council is not eligible under the fit and proper criteria.

cards.question: A non-executive director of a private sector bank has served eight years in total. When can the same bank re-appoint them?
options: Only after a gap of at least three years
Immediately, if shareholders approve at the AGM
After one year, with RBI's prior approval
Never, under any circumstances
cards.explanation: Paragraph 44(viii) caps total NED tenure at eight years, after which re-appointment needs a gap of at least three years. Serving on another bank's board is not barred.

cards.title: Stage three: the Boardroom
items: Banks must design need-based training for directors, and the Board must keep directors current on techniques, technology, markets and risk systems.
Public sector bank directors are familiarised with powers, strategy, structure, controls and the market before induction.
In private sector banks the NRC tests directors on qualification, expertise, track record and integrity using a signed declaration.
Interested NRC members stay out of the due diligence; annual declarations and a certificate to RBI keep it continuous.
RBI's 2020 actions on Yes Bank and Lakshmi Vilas Bank show how governance failures can end in a superseded Board.

cards.prompt: If you sat on a bank's board, which topic would you most want in your next need-based training session, and why does it matter for the bank's risk today?

quiz.question: Which body does paragraph 58 of the Miscellaneous Directions make responsible for ensuring directors are exposed to the latest managerial techniques, technology, markets and risk systems?
options: The Compliance Department
The Indian Banks' Association
The Board of the bank
RBI's Department of Supervision
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 58 gives this duty to the Board, while the bank designs need-based training programmes. RBI and IBA are not given the task.

quiz.question: A foreign bank operating through branches in India asks whether paragraph 58 director training applies to it. What is the answer?
options: It applies in full, with an annual certificate to RBI
It applies only to the foreign bank's Indian CCO
It applies only if the foreign bank has more than four branches
RBI says the requirement is not insisted upon for foreign banks
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 58 ends with a proviso that the requirement will not be insisted upon for foreign banks. The other conditions are invented.

quiz.question: Before a new director of a public sector bank is inducted, which area must the familiarisation cover under the Governance Directions?
options: The delegation of powers by the Board to various authorities
The personal credit history of each existing director
The salary structure of branch staff in each region
The bank's advertising plans for the next festival season
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 9 lists delegation of powers, strategic plan, organisation structure, financial and other controls and systems, and the market and competitive environment.

quiz.question: Who scrutinises the declarations of proposed directors of a private sector bank and decides on acceptance?
options: The Audit Committee of the Board
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee
The Chief Compliance Officer
The bank's statutory auditor
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 43 gives this task to the NRC, which may make references to appropriate authorities. The CCO and auditors do not decide on director suitability.

quiz.question: An NRC member seconded a candidate's name for appointment as director. What do the Governance Directions require?
options: That member leads the due diligence because they know the candidate best
That member stays out of the due diligence on that candidate, and the Board nominates another director as a temporary NRC member
The whole NRC is dissolved and the shareholders carry out the due diligence
The candidate must wait one year before being considered again
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 43(iii) excludes a proposer or seconder from the due diligence on that person and asks the Board to name a temporary member. The other options are not in the Directions.

quiz.question: Which factor do the Governance Directions list for assessing a private sector bank director's integrity and suitability?
options: The number of social media followers the candidate has
Whether the candidate lives in the same city as the head office
The candidate's previous salary in the private sector
Sanctions applied by regulators or similar bodies
quiz.explanation: The proviso to paragraph 43 lists criminal records, financial position, civil actions over personal debts, professional body expulsions, regulatory sanctions and questionable business practices.

quiz.question: A private sector bank is choosing a non-executive director aged 76 who is highly experienced. What do the fit and proper criteria say?
options: Eligible, because the age limits apply only to executive directors
Eligible if the NRC records special reasons in its minutes
Not eligible: the upper age limit for non-executive directors, including the Chair, is 75
Eligible for one term only, after which the 75-year limit applies
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 44(i) sets a minimum age of 35 and an upper limit of 75 for NEDs including the Chair, and no one can continue after 75. The NRC cannot override it.

quiz.question: What must a private sector bank obtain from each director as on 31 March every year?
options: A deed of covenant and a declaration that the information given earlier has not changed
A fresh university degree certificate and a new police report
A certificate from RBI confirming the director's continued eligibility
A letter from the CCO approving the director's continued membership
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 45 requires the deed of covenant and a simple declaration each 31 March, with details obtained at once if anything has changed. The bank then certifies continuing due diligence to RBI.

quiz.question: Under the Banking Regulation Act as reflected in the Governance Directions, what share of a banking company's Board must have special knowledge or practical experience in listed fields?
options: Not less than one-third
Exactly half
Not less than 75 per cent
Not less than 51 per cent
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 44(iii) refers to Section 10A(2)(a): not less than 51 per cent of the Board must have special knowledge or experience in fields such as accountancy, agriculture, banking, finance, law, IT and risk management.

quiz.question: RBI's press releases on Yes Bank (March 2020) and Lakshmi Vilas Bank (November 2020) both mentioned which problem?
options: Serious governance issues and practices in recent years
Cyber attacks that shut down core banking for several weeks
Failure to appoint a Head of Internal Audit for two years
Mis-selling of insurance products by branch staff
quiz.explanation: Both press releases cited serious governance issues and practices alongside financial deterioration, and both banks' Boards were superseded for 30 days. Neither release cited cyber attacks or mis-selling.

sessions.title: Internal Audit, Certified Staff and Sensitive Posts
sessions.summary: How risk-based internal audit works under RBI's 2026 Directions, why auditors must be competent and trained, which specialised posts need certification before posting, and how mandatory leave and staff rotation are checked.
objectives: Explain risk-based internal audit and the independence of the Internal Audit function
Describe RBI's expectations on internal auditors' competence and periodic training
List the specialised areas where staff need a certificate course before posting
Apply the mandatory leave and staff rotation rules that auditors must test

cards.title: The auditor who never saw a derivative
cards.setting: Internal Audit Department, Hyderabad. Annual audit planning week.

lines.text: Fatima Sheikh, Head of Internal Audit. Our treasury is now trading products none of my auditors has ever audited.
And the new dealer in treasury joined from a branch last week. Did anyone check whether he holds the certificate we need?
Good questions. RBI's audit Directions want skilled auditors trained periodically, and the Miscellaneous Directions want certification before posting to treasury.
Thomas here. My cash officer hasn't taken a day off in two years. She says the branch would collapse without her.
That is exactly what my auditors should be catching. Stage four: let's follow the audit trail.

cards.title: Risk-based internal audit in five scenes

scenes.heading: Risk first
scenes.narration: RBI requires commercial banks to use risk-based internal audit. It looks at risk management and controls, not just individual transactions, and spends audit effort where risk is highest.

scenes.heading: Board approvals
scenes.narration: The Board approves the audit policy, the risk assessment method and the annual audit plan, and may delegate the method and the plan to the Audit Committee.

scenes.heading: Independent
scenes.narration: The Internal Audit Department stays independent of the controls it checks and is not given accounting or operational work.

scenes.heading: The risk matrix
scenes.narration: Each activity is rated on inherent business risk and control risk. Where both are high, the area is extremely high risk and needs full transaction testing and top management's attention.

scenes.heading: Not outsourced
scenes.narration: Banks must not outsource the internal audit function. They may hire experts on contract when the Audit Committee is satisfied the skill is missing in-house, but regular staff own the reports.

cards.title: Reading the risk matrix
cards.caption: Selected cells from the illustrative matrix in the Internal Audit Function Directions, 2026.

items.label: High inherent, low control
items.detail: High risk: the business itself is risky even with good controls

items.label: High inherent, high control
items.detail: Extremely high risk: immediate audit attention and 100 per cent transaction testing

items.label: Low inherent, low control
items.detail: Low risk: audited at longer intervals, possibly with surprise checks

items.label: Low inherent, high control
items.detail: High risk: weak controls make even a simple activity dangerous

cards.question: A trade finance desk is rated high on inherent business risk and high on control risk. What does the illustrative risk matrix call for?
options: Extremely high risk: immediate audit attention, maximum audit resources and 100 per cent transaction testing
Medium risk: audit at the normal interval with sample testing
Low risk, because high control risk means many controls are in place
No audit until the next RBI inspection confirms the risk rating
cards.explanation: Cell C of the matrix combines high inherent and high control risk, making it extremely high risk, with 100 per cent transaction testing. High control risk means weak controls, not many controls.

cards.title: Competent, trained and independent auditors
cards.body:
**Resources and skills (para 14):** the bank gives Internal Audit enough resources and staff. Each auditor needs the right **professional competence, knowledge and experience**, and auditors should be **trained periodically** on the bank's business, operating procedures, risk management, control systems and MIS. Useful areas include banking operations, accounting, IT, data analytics and forensic investigation. The function must be able to audit **every area** of the bank.

**Staffing (para 7):** the Board sets a minimum period of service in Internal Audit (unless the bank uses career auditors) and may consider making staff with useful specialist skills serve at least one stint in audit.

**Pay (para 15):** audit pay is not linked to the financial results of the business lines audited.

**Retired staff (para 4):** a Board policy may allow retired personnel to be engaged for up to three years where expertise is lacking.

**Head of Internal Audit:** a senior executive with no business reporting line or targets, preferably appointed for at least three years, reporting to the ACB, MD & CEO or a whole-time director. Where the MD & CEO or WTD is the reporting authority, the ACB meets the HIA at least quarterly without senior management.

cards.title: Who audits what, and how
cards.prompt: Match each Internal Audit rule to its purpose.

pairs.right: Keeps auditors able to understand business, procedures, risk, controls and MIS
Keeps ownership of audit findings with the bank's own audit staff

pairs.left: Pay not tied to audited business
pairs.right: Avoids conflicts that could soften findings

pairs.left: Compliance risk in the audit plan
pairs.right: Lets Internal Audit test whether the compliance function works
Gives the auditor a safe channel to raise sensitive findings

cards.title: The dealer without a certificate
cards.setting: Treasury dealing room, Mumbai. Monday morning.

lines.text: Treasury is short-staffed. I've moved Kiran from the branch to the dealing desk today. He's sharp; he'll pick it up.
Has Kiran completed the certificate course our Board-approved policy requires for dealers?
He has enrolled. The exam is in two months. Can't he deal in the meantime?
The Directions say the certificate comes before the posting, not after. My auditors will test exactly this.

cards.title: Posting Kiran to the dealing desk
cards.situation: Kiran is capable but has not yet completed the certificate course that Sahyadri Crest Bank's Board-approved certification policy lists for treasury dealers. Treasury is short of one dealer, and Aditya wants him on the desk today.

choices.text: Keep Kiran off the dealing role until he is certified, cover the gap with a certified dealer, and fast-track his course.
choices.outcome: Best. The Miscellaneous Directions make a certificate course mandatory before posting in treasury dealing. Covering with certified staff keeps the desk running within the rules.

choices.text: Post him now under close supervision by a senior dealer until the exam.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Supervision lowers risk, but posting before certification still breaches the requirement and the bank's own policy.

choices.text: Post him and record that he has enrolled, which counts as certification.
choices.outcome: Poor. Enrolment is not certification. Auditors would treat this as a breach, and the record would mislead them.

cards.title: Certificate before posting?
cards.prompt: Sort each role by whether RBI's Miscellaneous Directions list it as needing a certificate course before posting.

items.text: Treasury dealer or mid-office officer
Credit appraisal and rating officer
Information security risk officer
Staff preparing the bank's financial results
Officer selling third-party wealth products
Internal audit function staff
Branch receptionist
Canteen manager at head office

cards.title: Certification and sensitive posts: the rules
Running a mandatory leave check
cards.prompt: Put the steps of the mandatory leave process in a sensible order.
steps: The Board or its committee approves the policy and the list of sensitive positions
HR picks the officer and the timing without telling the officer in advance
The officer goes on leave for at least 10 working days in one spell
IT removes the officer's access to work systems except general corporate email
Someone else handles the desk, and unusual items surface
Internal or concurrent auditors examine compliance and report any breach

cards.title: From skills to assurance
cards.caption: How competence rules feed reliable audit and control.

items.label: Certified staff in key posts
items.detail: Specialised posts are filled only with certified people

items.label: Trained auditors
items.detail: Auditors trained periodically on business, risk, controls and MIS

items.label: Risk-based audit plan
items.detail: Audit effort follows inherent and control risk

items.label: Tested controls
items.detail: Leave, rotation and compliance are examined and breaches reported

items.label: Assurance to the Board
items.detail: Serious findings reach the ACB promptly

cards.question: Thomas's cash officer is in a sensitive position and has not taken leave for two years. What should the internal auditor do?
options: Accept the branch's explanation that she is indispensable and close the point
Report the breach regardless of the reasons given, and examine the decisions and transactions she handled
Ask HR to give her one day off before the audit report is signed
Report it only if a fraud has already been found at the branch
cards.explanation: Paragraph 63B asks auditors to point out breaches irrespective of apparent justifications and to examine the decisions and transactions of staff not sent on leave. Waiting for a fraud defeats the purpose.

cards.title: Stage four: the Audit Trail
items: Commercial banks run risk-based internal audit, with a Board-approved policy, risk assessment method and annual audit plan.
Internal audit is independent, is not outsourced and is led by a Head of Internal Audit with no business targets.
Auditors need professional competence and periodic training on business, procedures, risk, controls and MIS.
Staff need a certificate course before posting to treasury, risk management, accounting and audit, credit management or third-party product sales.
Sensitive posts carry unannounced mandatory leave of at least 10 working days a year, and auditors test leave and rotation.

cards.prompt: Which post in your own team would you treat as sensitive, and what might a surprise period of leave reveal about how that work is done?

quiz.question: What is the main focus of risk-based internal audit under RBI's 2026 Directions?
options: Checking every transaction at every branch once a year, regardless of risk
Designing the bank's credit policies and approving large loans
Reasonable assurance to the Board and senior management on the adequacy and effectiveness of risk management and controls
Running the bank's compliance testing programme on behalf of the CCO
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 9 says RBIA gives reasonable assurance on risk management and controls. Audit does not design policies or approve loans, and compliance testing belongs to the compliance function.

quiz.question: Which statement on outsourcing internal audit matches the 2026 Directions?
options: The whole function may be outsourced to a chartered accountant firm approved by the Board
The function must not be outsourced, though experts may be hired on contract when the ACB is satisfied the skill is missing in-house
Outsourcing is allowed for branch audits but not for head office audits
Outsourcing is allowed if RBI is informed within thirty days
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 31 bars outsourcing the internal audit function but allows contract experts, including former employees, when expertise is lacking. Ownership of reports stays with regular audit staff.

quiz.question: According to paragraph 14 of the Internal Audit Function Directions, what should internal auditors be trained on periodically?
options: Only accounting standards, since audit is an accounting task
The bank's business activities, operating procedures, risk management, control systems and MIS
Sales techniques, so they understand business pressures
Only the RBI inspection manual used by supervisors
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 14 lists business activities, procedures, risk management, control systems and MIS, with useful areas such as operations, accounting, IT, data analytics and forensics.

quiz.question: The MD & CEO is the reporting authority of the Head of Internal Audit. What safeguard applies?
options: The CCO writes the HIA's appraisal to keep the two functions aligned
The HIA must also report to the Head of Retail Banking on branch findings
The ACB reviews the HIA's appraisal, the Board accepts it, and the ACB meets the HIA at least quarterly without senior management
RBI approves the HIA's annual appraisal before it is finalised
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 37 sets the ACB as reviewing authority and the Board as accepting authority, with quarterly ACB meetings without senior management. The CCO and business heads have no role.

quiz.question: An area has medium inherent business risk and high control risk, with risks increasing. What does the illustrative guidance suggest?
options: Treat it like an extremely high-risk area: immediate audit attention and maximum resources, with 100 per cent testing considered
Audit it at the longest permitted interval because inherent risk is only medium
Leave it to the Compliance Department, since control risk is a compliance matter
Rate it low risk because the trend will correct itself
quiz.explanation: Cell F (medium inherent, high control) is very high risk; with an increasing trend it needs the same attention as cell C, and banks may consider 100 per cent transaction testing.

quiz.question: A bank wants to post a branch officer to credit appraisal. What do the Miscellaneous Directions require?
options: The officer may be posted and must certify within one year
No certificate is needed for credit, only for treasury
The officer needs RBI's approval before the posting
The officer must acquire a certificate course in that area before the posting
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 59 lists credit management (appraisal, rating, monitoring, administration) among areas where a certificate course is mandatory before posting.

quiz.question: How does a bank decide which certification courses to accept for specialised areas?
options: RBI prescribes one compulsory course for every area each year
It picks suitable courses from those recognised by IBA and sets them in a Board-approved policy
Each department head chooses any course they consider useful
Only courses run by the bank's own training college count
quiz.explanation: Paragraphs 7 and 60 require a Board-approved policy (approval may be delegated to a Board committee) using courses recognised by IBA. Relevant university courses may also be considered.

quiz.question: What is the minimum mandatory leave for staff in sensitive positions?
options: At least 5 working days each quarter, announced a month in advance
At least 10 working days in total each year, taken in any number of spells
At least 15 calendar days every two years, at a time the employee chooses
At least 10 working days in a single spell each year, without prior intimation
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 62 requires leave of not less than 10 working days in one spell every year, without prior notice, to keep an element of surprise. Splitting the leave defeats the purpose.

quiz.question: While on mandatory leave, which access may a treasury officer keep?
options: Read-only access to the dealing system to monitor positions
Remote access to approve urgent payments
Internal corporate email that is generally available to all employees
Full access, provided a supervisor watches the activity
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 63 removes access to physical and virtual resources linked to work responsibilities, except general internal or corporate email.

quiz.question: Why may the Board ask staff with specialist skills in other departments to serve at least one stint in Internal Audit?
options: So that the Internal Audit function has adequate skills to audit specialised areas
So that business departments can influence audit findings on their areas
To reduce the number of staff who need certification
Because RBI requires every officer to work in audit before promotion
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7 lets the Board consider at least one stint in audit for staff with specialised knowledge useful to audit, so the function has adequate skills. It is not a universal promotion rule.

sessions.title: Speaking Up, Workplace Conduct and Assessment Readiness
sessions.summary: How to raise and handle whistle-blower concerns about possible fraud, how staff accountability works under RBI's 2026 fraud Directions, what the POSH Act means for a bank in general terms, and a recap of the compliance programme RBI will examine.
objectives: Explain the RBI expectation of a transparent whistle-blower mechanism for fraud concerns
Describe time-bound staff accountability in fraud cases, including for senior executives
Outline in general terms the employer's duties under the POSH Act, 2013
Recap the compliance programme, roles, reviews and records RBI expects to see

lines.text: An anonymous message reaches the bank's whistle-blower channel: loans at one branch are being sanctioned against valuation reports that look copied.
Thomas here. I think the note is about a branch near mine. Staff are scared that whoever wrote it will be found and punished.
It is probably a disgruntled employee. Can we not just close it?
No. RBI's 2026 fraud Directions require a transparent mechanism so that whistle-blower complaints on possible fraud are examined and concluded properly.
And if it is true, staff accountability must be examined in a time-bound way. Let's handle this right.

scenes.heading: A transparent mechanism
scenes.narration: RBI's Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026 require each bank to examine and conclude whistle-blower complaints about possible fraud or suspicious account activity through a transparent mechanism under its Whistle Blower Policy.

scenes.heading: Part of the fraud policy
scenes.narration: The bank's Board-approved fraud risk policy covers prevention, early detection, investigation, staff accountability, monitoring, recovery and reporting. The Board reviews it at least once in three years.

scenes.heading: A senior owner
scenes.narration: An official of at least General Manager rank is responsible for monitoring and reporting frauds, and a special Board committee oversees fraud risk management.

scenes.heading: Accountability on time
scenes.narration: The bank must start and finish examining staff accountability in every fraud case within a set time, under its internal policy.

scenes.heading: Protect the messenger
scenes.narration: Good whistle-blower policies keep the reporter's identity confidential and protect them from retaliation. Check your bank's policy for the exact channels and protections.

cards.title: Handling a whistle-blower complaint on possible fraud
cards.caption: A typical flow under a bank's Whistle Blower Policy, built around paragraph 10 of the 2026 fraud Directions.

items.label: Receive and log
items.detail: Record the complaint in the designated channel and protect the reporter's identity

items.label: Assess
items.detail: Decide whether it concerns possible fraud or suspicious account activity

items.label: Examine
items.detail: Investigate independently of the people named, gathering records and evidence

items.label: Conclude and record
items.detail: Reach a documented conclusion through the transparent mechanism

items.label: Act
items.detail: Report fraud as RBI requires, fix controls and examine staff accountability on time

cards.question: What does paragraph 10 of RBI's Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026 require about whistle-blower complaints?
options: That every complaint is sent directly to RBI within seven days
A transparent mechanism so complaints on possible fraud or suspicious account activity are examined and concluded under the Whistle Blower Policy
