That anonymous complaints are ignored unless the reporter gives a name
That the branch manager named in the complaint investigates it first
cards.explanation: Paragraph 10 asks for a transparent mechanism under the bank's own Whistle Blower Policy. It does not route complaints straight to RBI, and letting a named manager investigate would defeat independence.

cards.title: Staff accountability in fraud cases
cards.body:
**All fraud cases:** the bank starts and completes the examination of staff accountability **in a time-bound manner** under its internal policy.

**Public sector banks** follow the **Central Vigilance Commission's** guidelines and refer fraud cases of **₹3 crore and above** to the CVC's **Advisory Board for Banking and Financial Frauds** to examine the role of officials and whole-time directors.

**Very senior executives** (MD & CEO, Executive Directors and equivalents): the **Audit Committee** starts the examination and places it before the Board. These executives **do not take part** in meetings where their accountability is considered.

**Oversight:** a Special Committee of the Board for Monitoring and Follow-up of cases of Frauds, with at least three directors including a whole-time director and at least two independent or non-executive directors, reviews fraud cases, root causes and delays in staff accountability.

This links back to the compliance Directions: **staff accountability for compliance failures** is part of the culture RBI expects.

cards.title: Handling the anonymous note
cards.situation: The note names no one but describes copied valuation reports at a specific branch. Aditya wants to close it as 'unverified'. The regional head of that branch has offered to look into it himself.

choices.text: Log it, protect the source, have an independent team examine the loan files and valuations, conclude in writing and escalate any fraud under the fraud policy.
choices.outcome: Best. This is the transparent examination and conclusion RBI expects, independent of those who may be involved, with fraud reporting and staff accountability to follow if the concern is confirmed.

choices.text: Ask the regional head to check quietly and report back.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Something gets examined, but the person checking may be connected to the branch and the outcome may not be documented transparently.

choices.text: Close it because the reporter is anonymous and gave no names.
choices.outcome: Poor. The complaint is specific enough to examine. Closing it unread breaks the transparent mechanism RBI requires and could hide a fraud.

choices.text: Try to identify the writer first to judge their motives.
choices.outcome: Poor. Hunting for the reporter discourages speaking up and risks retaliation. The facts, not the motive, decide the outcome.

cards.title: Workplace conduct: the POSH Act in brief
cards.body:
The **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013** (often called the **POSH Act**) applies to employers in India, including banks.

**In general terms, the Act:**
- prohibits sexual harassment of women at the workplace;
- requires employers to set up an **Internal Committee** to receive and inquire into complaints;
- places duties on employers to provide a safe working environment and to make staff aware of the law and how to complain.

**What it means for you:** know who sits on your bank's Internal Committee and how to reach it, treat every complaint seriously and confidentially, and never retaliate against a complainant or witness.

This quest covers the Act only in outline, because its official text could not be opened for checking. **Follow your bank's POSH policy and training** for the exact procedures, timelines and committee details.

cards.title: Speak-up channel or POSH Internal Committee?
cards.prompt: Sort each concern to the channel it most naturally belongs to at a bank.

items.text: Valuation reports appear copied across several loan files
A colleague receives repeated unwelcome sexual remarks from a supervisor
Suspicious round-tripping of funds in a customer's account
A senior officer seems to be overriding controls to favour a borrower
A request for physical favours in exchange for a better posting
A disagreement over shift rosters
A request for training on a new software tool

cards.title: Getting ready for RBI
cards.setting: CCO's office, Mumbai. Two weeks before RBI's supervisory visit.

lines.text: RBI's team arrives soon. They will want to see that our compliance programme works, not just that it exists.
The Audit Committee will want the quarterly reviews, the annual review and proof that last cycle's action points are closed.
My team has audited the compliance function itself this year. I'll share the findings with you, as the Directions expect.
And my branch can finally show training completion above ninety per cent!
Then let's assemble the evidence. Final stage: prove the culture is real.

cards.title: Evidence RBI may ask for
cards.caption: Assembled from the Compliance Function, Internal Audit, Miscellaneous and Fraud Directions.

items.label: Policy
items.left: Board-approved compliance policy reviewed in the past year
items.right: Board minutes and policy version history

items.label: Oversight
items.left: Quarterly and annual compliance reviews with the CCO invited
items.right: Board or ACB papers and minutes

items.label: Training
items.left: Continuous, mandatory compliance training for all staff
items.right: Learning records, completion and assessment data

items.label: Supervisory points
items.left: MAP or RMP items closed on time and sustained
items.right: Compliance tool records and validation evidence

items.label: Key posts
items.left: Certified staff in specialised areas; mandatory leave taken

cards.title: Who does what: final recap
cards.prompt: Match each role to its key responsibility from this quest.

pairs.right: Oversees compliance risk, keeps directors trained and approves the compliance and certification policies
Tests directors against fit and proper criteria using signed declarations
Leads an independent compliance function and is the bank's nodal contact with RBI
Leads independent risk-based audit, including audit of the compliance function
Completes compliance training, follows instructions and speaks up about possible fraud

cards.title: The Directions behind this quest
cards.caption: Dates as shown on RBI's website.

items.label: Governance and Miscellaneous Directions
items.detail: Consolidated Directions for commercial banks, effective immediately

items.label: Compliance Function Directions
items.detail: Compliance culture, CCO, mandatory training; effective on issue

items.label: Internal Audit Function Directions
items.detail: Risk-based internal audit and auditor competence; effective on issue

items.label: Fraud Risk Management Directions
items.detail: Fraud policy, whistle-blower mechanism, staff accountability; effective on issue

cards.front: Who reviews the compliance function every quarter?
cards.back: The Board or the Audit Committee of the Board, with a detailed annual review as well.

cards.front: Can compliance staff do branch inspections?
cards.back: No. Compliance staff must never be given audit or inspection duty.

cards.front: How often is the compliance QA programme externally reviewed?
cards.back: Independently and externally, at least once in three years.

cards.front: How often does the Board review the fraud risk policy?
cards.back: At least once in three years, or more often if the Board decides.

cards.front: PSB fraud cases referred to the CVC's ABBFF?
cards.back: Cases of ₹3 crore and above, to examine the role of officials and whole-time directors.

cards.question: RBI asks Sahyadri Crest Bank how it knows the compliance function itself works. Which evidence fits the 2026 Directions best?
options: A self-assessment by the CCO with no outside review
A letter from the Head of Retail Banking praising the CCO
Internal Audit's review of the compliance function, shared with the CCO, plus the external QA review
Compliance staff inspecting their own branch work
cards.explanation: Paragraphs 53 and 54 subject the compliance function to internal audit (with findings shared with the CCO) and to a periodic independent external review of its QA programme. Self-review and business praise are not independent.

cards.title: Stage five: the Open Door
items: Banks need a transparent mechanism to examine and conclude whistle-blower complaints on possible fraud under their Whistle Blower Policy.
Staff accountability in fraud cases is examined in a time-bound way; for very senior executives, the ACB starts it and the Board decides.
The POSH Act, 2013 requires employers to prevent sexual harassment and set up an Internal Committee; follow your bank's POSH policy for details.
RBI will look for evidence: reviewed policies, quarterly and annual reviews, training records, closed supervisory points and audited compliance.

cards.prompt: Where would you raise a concern about possible fraud at your bank today, and what would make you more confident that speaking up is safe and taken seriously?

quiz.question: Under RBI's Fraud Risk Management Directions, 2026, how must whistle-blower complaints on possible fraud be handled?
options: Forwarded unread to the police, since banks may not investigate fraud themselves
Accepted only if the reporter signs the complaint and gives a phone number
Investigated by the manager of the unit named in the complaint
Examined and concluded appropriately through a transparent mechanism under the bank's Whistle Blower Policy
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 10 requires a transparent mechanism under the Whistle Blower Policy. Requiring the reporter's identity or using the named manager would undermine it.

quiz.question: How often must the Board review the bank's Fraud Risk Management Policy at a minimum?
options: At least once in three years
At least once a year
Only after a fraud above ₹3 crore
At least once every five years
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7 sets a review at least once in three years, or more often as the Board decides. The annual cycle applies to the compliance policy, not the fraud policy.

quiz.question: A fraud case involves possible lapses by the MD & CEO. Who starts the examination of the MD & CEO's accountability?
options: The MD & CEO, who reports on their own conduct to the Board
The Audit Committee of the Board, which places it before the Board
The Chief Compliance Officer, who decides on any penalty
The branch where the fraud was discovered
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 38 gives this to the ACB, which places it before the Board; the executive concerned does not take part in those meetings. Public sector banks also refer such cases to the ABBFF.

quiz.question: A public sector bank finds a fraud of ₹5 crore. Beyond its own examination, where must it refer the case to examine officials' roles?
options: The RBI Ombudsman for the region where the fraud occurred
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the bank
The Advisory Board for Banking and Financial Frauds set up by the Central Vigilance Commission
The Indian Banks' Association's disciplinary committee
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 37 requires PSBs to follow CVC guidelines and refer fraud cases of ₹3 crore and above to the ABBFF. The Ombudsman handles customer complaints, not staff accountability.

quiz.question: What is the minimum composition of the Special Committee of the Board for Monitoring and Follow-up of cases of Frauds?
options: Two members: the MD & CEO and the CCO
Five members, all of them independent directors
Any three senior executives chosen by the MD & CEO
Three Board members: a whole-time director and at least two independent or non-executive directors
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 8 sets at least three Board members, including a whole-time director and at least two independent or non-executive directors, chaired by one of the independent or non-executive directors.

quiz.question: Which statement about the POSH Act, 2013 is accurate at the general level this quest covers?
options: It applies only to government departments, not to private banks
It requires employers, including banks, to set up an Internal Committee to receive and inquire into complaints
It is administered by RBI through its Compliance Function Directions
It allows complaints only through the bank's whistle-blower channel
quiz.explanation: The POSH Act applies to employers generally, including banks, and requires an Internal Committee. It is not an RBI instrument and has its own complaint route.

quiz.question: A colleague confides that a supervisor keeps making unwelcome sexual remarks. What is the most appropriate first step for you?
options: Report it on the fraud whistle-blower channel as suspicious account activity
Confront the supervisor publicly at the next team meeting
Tell her about the bank's Internal Committee and how to reach it, keep it confidential and support her
Advise her to wait and see whether it stops on its own
quiz.explanation: Sexual harassment complaints belong with the Internal Committee under the POSH Act and the bank's POSH policy. The fraud channel is for possible fraud; confronting publicly or waiting can cause harm.

quiz.question: Which rule links staff accountability across RBI's compliance and fraud Directions?
options: Banks must examine staff accountability for compliance failures and, in a time-bound way, for fraud cases
Staff accountability applies only to officers above General Manager rank
Staff accountability is examined only after RBI imposes a penalty
Staff accountability is replaced by training once a breach is found
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 44 of the Compliance Directions requires accountability for all compliance failures; paragraph 36 of the Fraud Directions requires time-bound examination in all fraud cases. Neither is limited by rank or by RBI penalties.

quiz.question: Preparing for RBI's visit, the CCO wants evidence that compliance training is real. Which evidence is strongest?
options: A copy of the training slides stored on the intranet
An email from the CCO reminding staff that training exists
A list of trainers' names and their qualifications
Learning records showing completion and assessment results for all staff, with follow-up of those who missed it
quiz.explanation: RBI expects continuous and mandatory training for all staff; records of completion and assessment show it happened. Slides or reminders only show that material exists.

quiz.question: Who must the Internal Audit function keep informed of audit findings related to compliance?
options: The Head of Retail Banking
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee
The Chief Compliance Officer
RBI's Senior Supervisory Manager
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 54 of the Compliance Function Directions requires Internal Audit to keep the CCO informed of compliance-related audit findings.

regulators: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), for staff accountability in public sector banks

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Compliance Function) Directions, 2026
references.note: Compliance staff need suitable knowledge and regular education on laws, products and governance; all staff must be reminded periodically, through continuous and mandatory compliance training, of the need to comply, with disciplinary measures for non-compliance.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Compliance Function) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 6-27, 30-54 and 55-75 (Board, senior management, policy, structure, culture, CCO, technology)
references.note: Board oversight with quarterly and annual reviews, a Board-approved compliance policy reviewed yearly, compliance kept separate from internal audit, staff accountability for compliance failures, and a CCO with fixed tenure, no business targets, direct reporting and prior intimation to RBI on appointment or removal.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025
references.note: Banks must design need-based training programmes for directors, promote senior management awareness of security, risk and controls in computerised environments, and keep directors current on management, technology, markets and risk (not insisted on for foreign banks).

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025
references.provision: Paragraphs 7, 40 and 59-63B (circulars; certification before posting; mandatory leave and staff rotation)
references.note: RBI circulars must reach branches without delay; staff need a certificate course before posting to treasury, risk management, accounting and audit, credit management and third-party product sales; sensitive posts carry unannounced mandatory leave of at least 10 working days a year, checked by auditors.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025
references.provision: Paragraphs 9, 23-25 and 42-45 (PSB familiarisation; fit and proper criteria for PSB and private sector bank directors)
references.note: PSB directors are familiarised with the bank before induction; proposed directors give declarations that the Nomination and Remuneration Committee tests against fit and proper criteria; private sector banks renew declarations each year and certify continuing due diligence to RBI.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Internal Audit Function) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 4-17, 31 and 33-37 (RBIA governance; independence; staff competence and training; outsourcing; Head of Internal Audit)
references.note: Internal auditors need professional competence and should be trained periodically on business activities, operating procedures, risk management, control systems and MIS; the audit function stays independent, is not outsourced and is led by a Head of Internal Audit with no business targets.

references.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Fraud Risk Management) Directions, 2026
references.provision: Paragraphs 5-11 and 36-38 (fraud risk policy; whistle blower complaints; staff accountability)
references.note: Whistle blower complaints about possible frauds or suspicious account activity must be examined and concluded through a transparent mechanism under the bank's Whistle Blower Policy; staff accountability in fraud cases is examined in a time-bound way.

references.title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
references.note: Requires employers to set up an Internal Committee and to prevent and redress sexual harassment at work. India Code blocks automated access, so the text was not opened and the quest covers the Act only in general terms.

references.title: Action against Paytm Payments Bank Ltd under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (press release, 31 January 2024)
references.note: After a 2022 stop on onboarding new customers, external audit reports showed persistent non-compliances and continued material supervisory concerns, so RBI barred further deposits and credits after a cut-off date.

references.title: Supervisory Action against Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (press release, 24 April 2024)
references.note: RBI stopped online onboarding of new customers and new credit cards, citing IT examination concerns for 2022 and 2023 and compliance with corrective action plans that was inadequate, incorrect or not sustained.

references.title: Yes Bank Ltd. placed under Moratorium (press release, 5 March 2020)
references.note: RBI said the bank's steady decline followed its inability to raise capital and serious governance issues and practices in recent years; the Board was superseded for 30 days the same day (press release prid=49477).

references.title: The Lakshmi Vilas Bank Ltd. placed under Moratorium (press release, 17 November 2020)
references.note: RBI cited three years of losses, no viable strategic plan, mounting NPAs and serious governance issues and practices; the Board was superseded for 30 days and a draft amalgamation with DBS Bank India was published.

bank.question: A private sector commercial bank's Board has not reviewed its compliance policy for 20 months, though the ACB has reviewed the compliance function every quarter. What is the position under the 2026 Directions?
options: Compliant, because quarterly reviews of the function satisfy the policy review duty
A gap: quarterly function reviews do not replace the Board's own review of the policy at least once a year
Compliant, because the policy only needs review when RBI changes its Directions
A gap only if RBI has raised a specific observation on the policy
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7 requires the Board to review the compliance policy at least annually, while paragraph 9 separately requires quarterly reviews of the function. One does not satisfy the other.

bank.question: Which item must the Board-approved compliance policy cover under the 2026 Directions?
options: A sales incentive plan for compliance officers tied to branch deposit growth
A rule that the CCO also heads internal audit in smaller banks
A list of customers exempt from compliance checks because of their size
An approval process by the Compliance Department for all new processes and products before introduction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 17(11) lists prior approval of new products and processes by Compliance. Incentives tied to business, merging with audit and customer exemptions all contradict the Directions.

bank.question: Sahyadri Crest Bank distributes insurance as a corporate agent and receives a direction from IRDAI. How should the compliance function treat it?
options: As part of its remit, and bring any discomfort conveyed by other regulators to RBI's notice
Ignore it, because the compliance function deals only with RBI instructions
Pass it to the insurance company, which alone is responsible for compliance
Treat it as advisory unless RBI repeats the same direction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 50 makes compliance with other regulators' directions, such as IRDAI and SEBI, part of the compliance function and requires discomfort from other regulators to be reported to RBI.

bank.question: A branch keeps applying an outdated instruction because its operating manual was never updated. Which compliance policy element was most likely missing?
options: A selection committee to recommend candidates for the CCO post
A quarterly one-to-one meeting between the ACB and the CCO
A mechanism to disseminate regulatory directions to operational staff and update operating manuals periodically
A minimum fixed tenure for the Head of Internal Audit
bank.explanation: Paragraph 17(10) requires a mechanism to disseminate regulatory instructions and update operating manuals. The other items concern governance of the CCO and HIA, not field implementation.

bank.question: What must a bank disclose in its annual report under the 2026 Compliance Function Directions?
options: The names of all staff disciplined for compliance breaches during the year
Non-compliance with regulatory guidelines, administrative actions against the bank and corrective steps taken
The CCO's salary compared with business heads' salaries
Every customer complaint received and how it was resolved
bank.explanation: Paragraph 43 calls for disclosure of non-compliance, administrative actions and corrective steps in the annual report. Naming individual staff is not required.

bank.question: Which practice best shows the Compliance Department meeting paragraph 30 of the 2026 Directions?
options: Keeping all compliance failures confidential so staff morale is not affected
Reporting compliance failures only to RBI and not to the bank's own staff
Removing compliance failures from records once the staff member is disciplined
Periodically circulating instances of compliance failures to staff together with preventive instructions
bank.explanation: Paragraph 30 asks the Compliance Department to circulate instances of compliance failures among staff with preventive instructions, which is a core part of building culture.

bank.question: Two branch managers have equal sales results, but one had three compliance breaches. What does the 2026 Directions' approach to appraisal suggest?
options: Their appraisals must be equal because compliance is the Compliance Department's job
The manager with breaches must be dismissed under RBI's rules
Their compliance records may be given due weight, so the appraisals need not be equal
Compliance records can be considered only for staff in control functions
bank.explanation: Paragraph 44 says due weight may be given to compliance records in appraisals at all levels. It does not mandate dismissal, and it is not limited to control functions.

bank.question: The Compliance Function Directions, 2026 were issued under which statutory power?
options: Section 35-A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 12 of the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002
Section 36ACA of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
bank.explanation: The Directions state they are issued under Section 35-A of the Banking Regulation Act. Section 45 relates to moratorium and reconstruction, and Section 36ACA to supersession of a Board, as used for Yes Bank and LVB.

bank.question: Which statement best explains why RBI's January 2024 action on Paytm Payments Bank is a lesson for compliance culture?
options: Earlier restrictions and audit findings were followed by persistent non-compliances, so RBI escalated its action
The bank had no compliance department at all, which RBI discovered by chance
The bank had breached a capital rule only once, and RBI acted immediately
RBI acted because customers had complained about high fees
bank.explanation: The press release explains that after the March 2022 onboarding stop, audit and compliance validation reports showed persistent non-compliances and continued material supervisory concerns, leading to further restrictions.

bank.question: Under the 2026 Directions, who takes the final decision on appointing the CCO?
options: The MD & CEO alone, after consulting the Head of Internal Audit
The Board, after a senior executive selection committee recommends candidates in order of merit
RBI's Senior Supervisory Manager, who approves each candidate
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee, without the Board
bank.explanation: Paragraph 56 sets a Board-constituted senior executive selection committee recommending candidates in order of merit, with the Board deciding. RBI receives prior intimation but does not appoint.

bank.question: What must accompany the bank's prior intimation to RBI before appointing a new CCO?
options: A copy of the candidate's last three salary slips and a medical report
A letter from the outgoing CCO approving the successor
A detailed profile of the candidate and the MD & CEO's fit and proper certification
The minutes of the bank's annual general meeting
bank.explanation: Paragraph 70 asks for a detailed profile with the MD & CEO's fit and proper certification and the rationale for any change.

bank.question: Which candidate is barred from appointment as CCO regardless of experience?
options: A candidate recruited from outside the bank
A candidate who previously worked in the bank's risk department
A candidate aged 50 with 18 years in banking
A candidate with a vigilance case pending against them
bank.explanation: Paragraph 57 says no vigilance case or adverse RBI observation may be pending against the CCO candidate. Outside recruitment is expressly allowed.

bank.question: A small bank with a limited branch network wants its compliance staff to handle some other duties. What do the Directions allow?
options: Other duties are possible if there is no conflict of interest, but never audit or inspection duty
Any duties at all, including branch inspection, because the bank is small
No other duties of any kind, regardless of the bank's size
Other duties only if the CCO personally performs them
bank.explanation: Paragraph 24 lets small banks assign other duties without conflicts of interest, while barring audit and inspection duty under all circumstances.

bank.question: A large bank places compliance staff inside its business units, reporting locally. What else is required?
options: Nothing, because local management is accountable for compliance
Approval from RBI for each embedded compliance officer
That they also report to the Head of Internal Audit
A reporting line through to the CCO for their compliance responsibilities
bank.explanation: Paragraph 26 allows local reporting lines but requires a line through to the CCO for compliance responsibilities, keeping the function's coherence and independence.

bank.question: Which arrangement for compliance staff remuneration complies with the 2026 Directions?
options: A bonus based on the revenue of the business line each officer covers
Pay linked to the bank's overall financial performance, not to the business line they oversee
Pay set by the head of the business line each officer covers
Commission on new products the officer clears for launch
bank.explanation: Paragraph 27 separates compliance pay from the business line covered but allows a link to the bank's overall performance. Product-clearance commissions would create a direct conflict.

bank.question: What must the bank's compliance technology solution do under Chapter V of the 2026 Directions?
options: Replace the Compliance Department's staff with automated decision-making
Send every internal breach report directly to RBI in real time
Escalate non-compliance, record approvals for deviations or delays and give senior management a unified dashboard
Be bought from a vendor approved by RBI
bank.explanation: Paragraph 74 lists collaboration, processes for managing requirements, escalation, recorded approvals for deviations and delays, and a unified dashboard. The bank chooses the tools by size and complexity.

bank.question: To whom is the CCO's risk-oriented activity plan submitted for approval, and with whom is it shared?
options: Submitted to RBI for approval and shared with the statutory auditors
Submitted to the MD & CEO for approval and kept confidential
Submitted to business heads for approval and shared with branches
Submitted to the Audit Committee for approval and made available to Internal Audit
bank.explanation: Paragraph 71(3) requires the activity plan, based on at least annual compliance risk assessment, to be approved by the ACB and made available to the Internal Audit function.

bank.question: The MAP points from RBI's last risk-based supervision cycle are still open. What do the 2026 Directions expect?
options: A time-bound strategy to comply within the set periods and well before the next supervisory cycle begins
Closing them once RBI's next cycle starts, since inspectors will check them then
Closing them only if RBI imposes a penalty for delay
Delegating them to Internal Audit, which owns supervisory findings
bank.explanation: Paragraph 46 requires compliance units to devise a time-bound strategy and comply with MAP/RMP points well before the next supervisory cycle or within the set period.

bank.question: Which statement about paragraph 58 of the Miscellaneous Directions on directors is correct?
options: Directors must attend an RBI-run course within six months of appointment
The bank must also promote senior management's awareness of security, risk and controls in a computerised environment
Only executive directors need training; independent directors are exempt
Training must be delivered by the CCO in person every quarter
bank.explanation: Paragraph 58 covers need-based training for directors, senior management awareness of computerised-environment risks, and the Board's duty to keep directors current. It sets no RBI course or CCO delivery rule.

bank.question: The Board of Sahyadri Crest Bank wants the NRC to assess its own members' suitability as directors. What is the problem?
options: None, because the NRC assesses all directors including its own members
NRC members are exempt from fit and proper checks
Due diligence on NRC members must be done by the Board itself, as NRC members are interested parties
RBI must carry out due diligence on NRC members directly
bank.explanation: Paragraph 43(ii) assigns due diligence on NRC members to the Board, with those members excluded. They are not exempt, and RBI does not do it directly.

bank.question: A director of a non-banking financial institution is proposed as a director of a private sector bank. Which condition must be met?
options: The NBFI must be a borrower of the bank, so the bank understands its business
The person must hold more than half of the NBFI's shares
The person must first resign from all other boards
The NBFI must not be a borrower of the bank, and the person must not own it, be related to its promoter or be its full-time employee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 44(vi) sets these conditions: not the owner (not over 50 per cent), not related to the promoter, not a full-time employee, and the NBFI not a borrower of the bank.

bank.question: What age range applies to candidates for elected director of a public sector bank?
options: Between 35 and 67 years on the cut-off date for nominations
Between 25 and 70 years on the date of the election
Between 35 and 75 years, the same as private sector bank NEDs
No age limit, provided the candidate is a graduate
bank.explanation: Paragraph 25(i) sets 35 to 67 for PSB elected directors. The 35 to 75 range applies to private sector bank NEDs.

bank.question: As a matter of desirable practice, what do the Governance Directions say about family members on a bank's Board?
options: Up to three family members may serve if they are all independent
Family members may serve only as whole-time directors
Not more than one member of a family, close relative or associate should be on the Board
There is no guidance on family members
bank.explanation: Paragraph 44(vii) states, as desirable practice, that not more than one member of a family or a close relative or associate may be on the Board.

bank.question: A private sector bank finds that a director's information changed in September, but the director plans to tell the bank next 31 March. What should happen?
options: Nothing until 31 March, when the annual declaration is due
The bank should obtain the updated details from the director immediately, not wait for the annual declaration
The director must resign and seek re-appointment
The bank reports the change to RBI and takes no other step
bank.explanation: Paragraph 45 requires the annual covenant and declaration, but where information changes the bank must obtain details forthwith.

bank.question: What is the most accurate governance lesson from RBI's supersession of the Yes Bank Board in March 2020?
options: A bank's Board can be superseded only if the bank commits a cyber security breach
Supersession is automatic whenever a bank's share price falls
Supersession is used only for co-operative banks, not private sector banks
Weak governance and a failure to produce a credible revival plan can lead RBI to replace the Board
bank.explanation: RBI cited serious governance issues, inability to raise capital and the absence of a credible revival plan before superseding the Board for 30 days under the Banking Regulation Act.

bank.question: In the Lakshmi Vilas Bank case of November 2020, which step did RBI take alongside the moratorium and supersession of the Board?
options: It published a draft scheme to merge the bank with State Bank of India
It published a draft scheme to amalgamate the bank with DBS Bank India
It cancelled the bank's licence the same day
It required every director to retake the fit and proper test within a week
bank.explanation: RBI's 17 November 2020 releases announced the moratorium, a 30-day supersession and a draft amalgamation with DBS Bank India Ltd. SBI was the investor in the Yes Bank reconstruction, not LVB.

bank.question: Which pair does the Board (or Local Advisory Board of a foreign bank) approve, with power to delegate them to the Audit Committee?
options: The RBIA policy and the policy on engaging retired staff
The Head of Internal Audit's daily work allocation and leave
The risk assessment methodology and the annual audit plan
Individual audit reports for each branch
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4 lists the RBIA policy, the risk assessment methodology, the annual audit plan and the retired-personnel policy; only the methodology and the plan may be delegated to the ACB.

bank.question: A bank engages retired officers to help Internal Audit with a niche area. What does the Board policy need to respect?
options: A maximum engagement tenure of three years, with terms, performance review and termination set out
A minimum engagement of five years so the expertise is retained
Engagement only of officers who retired from the Compliance Department
RBI approval for each retired officer engaged
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4(4) allows a Board policy to engage retired personnel for up to three years where expertise is lacking, covering terms, performance review and termination.

bank.question: What must the Internal Audit Department's risk assessment cover at minimum frequency?
options: It must be done at least annually and updated periodically for changes in business and processes
Once every three years, aligned to the RBI supervisory cycle
Only when a new product is launched
Monthly, with RBI's approval of each update
bank.explanation: Paragraph 22 requires risk assessment at least annually, with periodic updates for changes in environment, activities and processes.

bank.question: Which item must risk-based internal audit review at minimum, under paragraph 26?
options: The marketing budget of each business line
Personal tax filings of senior executives
Gaps in control mechanisms that might lead to frauds, and fraud-prone areas
Customer satisfaction scores for each branch
bank.explanation: Paragraph 26 lists, among other things, control gaps that might lead to frauds and the identification of fraud-prone areas, together with compliance and MIS integrity.

bank.question: Fatima's auditors lack data analytics and forensic skills for a complex review. Which response fits the Internal Audit Directions best?
options: Outsource the whole review to a consultancy and adopt its report as the bank's own
Train auditors periodically and build these skills, hiring contract experts only if the ACB is assured the expertise is missing
Skip the review, since auditors need only accounting knowledge
Ask the Compliance Department to perform the review instead
bank.explanation: Paragraph 14 lists data analytics and forensic investigation as desirable areas and asks for periodic training; paragraph 31 allows contract experts under ACB assurance, with ownership of reports staying in-house.

bank.question: Under the Miscellaneous Directions, which role in risk management requires a certificate course before posting?
options: Branch facilities management
Corporate communications
Staff canteen supervision
Liquidity risk management
bank.explanation: Paragraph 59(2) covers credit, market, operational, enterprise-wide, information security and liquidity risk management.

bank.question: A relationship manager will sell third-party mutual funds. SEBI prescribes a certification for this. Which rule applies?
options: RBI's list does not cover third-party products, so only SEBI's rule applies
The bank's certification requirement applies, and where another regulator prescribes a certification, that must be complied with
The SEBI certification is optional if the RM holds a university degree
The RM may sell for one year before certification is checked
bank.explanation: Paragraph 59(5) covers marketing of third-party retail products and wealth management, and its proviso says certifications prescribed by other financial sector regulators must be complied with.

bank.question: An officer in a sensitive post was not sent on mandatory leave this year. Beyond reporting the breach, what must the internal or concurrent auditors do?
options: Comprehensively examine the decisions taken and transactions effected by that officer and document the findings
Nothing more, if the branch gives a reasonable explanation
Recommend the officer's dismissal to the Board
Inform RBI directly and suspend the audit
bank.explanation: Paragraph 63B asks auditors to point out breaches regardless of justifications and to examine and document the decisions and transactions of staff not rotated or not sent on leave.

bank.question: What must the Board-approved Fraud Risk Management Policy contain, among other things?
options: A guarantee that no fraud will occur once the policy is approved
Sales targets for the fraud monitoring team
A list of staff who may never be investigated
Measures for prevention, early detection, investigation, staff accountability, monitoring, recovery and reporting of frauds
bank.explanation: Paragraph 5 lists these elements, along with the early warning signals and red-flagging framework.

bank.question: Which official must be responsible for monitoring and reporting frauds under the 2026 fraud Directions?
options: Any branch manager nominated by the regional office
The statutory auditor appointed for the year
A senior official of at least General Manager rank or equivalent
The Chief Compliance Officer in every bank, without exception
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11 requires a senior official of at least General Manager rank or equivalent to be responsible for monitoring and reporting frauds. The Directions do not assign this to the CCO by default.

bank.question: A whistle-blower alleges a fraud that may involve the MD & CEO. How should the MD & CEO take part in the Board meeting that considers their accountability?
options: They chair the meeting to provide context
They vote, but their vote counts half
They attend and decide whether the matter goes to the ACB
They must not participate in that meeting
bank.explanation: Paragraph 38 says very senior executives whose accountability is being considered must not participate in the Board, ACB or SCBMF meeting concerned.

bank.question: What makes a whistle-blower process 'transparent' in the sense RBI's fraud Directions use, as applied in good practice?
options: Every complaint and the reporter's name are published on the intranet
Complaints are logged, examined independently of those named and concluded with documented reasons
The complaint is decided informally by the reporter's line manager
Only complaints with documentary proof are examined
bank.explanation: Transparency means a clear, recorded process to examine and conclude complaints, not exposing reporters. Publishing names would deter speaking up; requiring full proof would filter out genuine concerns.

bank.question: Which statement on the POSH Act, 2013 is within what this quest can state reliably?
options: The Act requires every complaint to be filed with RBI within ten days
The Act applies only to banks with more than 5,000 employees
Employers must set up an Internal Committee and work to prevent sexual harassment; the bank's POSH policy gives the detailed procedure
The Act replaced the need for any internal complaints committee at banks
bank.explanation: The quest covers the POSH Act only in general terms: an Internal Committee and a duty to prevent harassment. RBI does not receive POSH complaints, and the other statements are not part of the Act as described here.

bank.question: During RBI's visit, inspectors ask how the bank makes sure compliance staff themselves stay current. Which answer fits paragraph 29?
options: Through regular, systematic education on new products, governance, risk management and supervisory practice, on top of knowledge of law, accounting and IT
Compliance staff need no training because they write the training for others
Only the CCO needs updating; other compliance staff follow instructions
Compliance staff attend the general staff module, which is enough by itself
bank.explanation: Paragraph 29 expects compliance staff to have fair knowledge of law, accounting and IT and suggests regular, systematic education in new products, governance, risk management and supervisory practices.

bank.question: RBI asks how the bank tests whether its compliance function covers all RBI guidelines, given that RBS templates are not exhaustive. Which answer fits paragraph 45?
options: The bank complies only with items listed in the latest RBS template
The bank waits for RBI to flag gaps during the next inspection
The bank strives for an exhaustive compliance framework covering all RBI guidelines and remedies potential breaches up front
The bank relies on the statutory auditor to list applicable guidelines
bank.explanation: Paragraph 45 notes the templates are neither exhaustive nor static and asks banks to build an exhaustive framework covering all RBI guidelines and remedy breaches up front.

bank.question: Which combination best describes the three independent assurance layers around compliance at a commercial bank?
options: Compliance function testing, internal audit of the compliance function, and an external review of the compliance QA programme
Business line self-certification, sales reviews and customer surveys
The CCO's own review, the MD & CEO's review and the HR department's review
Statutory audit only, since it covers all compliance matters
bank.explanation: The Directions require compliance testing by the function (paragraph 39), internal audit of compliance (paragraph 54) and an independent external review of the QA programme at least once in three years (paragraph 53).
